A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ischemic myocardium is not a hospitable environment for transplanted cells.
the low engraftment rate of transplanted stem cells in ischemic myocardial tissues is a major obstacle for clinical translation of cellular therapies for ischemic heart diseases.

cell engraftments and cell survival in ischemic heart is a multifactorial problem, and the approaches that have shown the most promising results in preclinical studies include the combination of cell therapy with pharmacologic agents and the use of tissue engineering approaches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the poor survival of transplanted stem cells in ischemic myocardial is a multifactorial process, and that there is no single factor that can be used to improve cell engrafting and survival.

the ischemic microenvironment of the heart is hostile to transplanted cells, and that the poor engraftment/survival of transplanted stem cells in the ischemic setting can be attributed, at least in part, to the ischemic microvascular dysfunction.
